Data file path /sites/default/files/2026-05/lbnl_ix_queue_data_file_thru2025.xlsx on eta-publications.lbl.gov; server declares 15,571,236 bytes (Content-Length, GitHub Actions probe run 40580149328; not downloaded). The publication page's Last-Modified header differed between two reads on 2026-10-27, so it is not used as a release date.

sources.semantics: Project-level interconnection queue data file for projects seeking transmission interconnection as of end of 2025 (publisher description)
limitations: Data as of end of 2025: a snapshot, not a forecast
Queue statistic is not a data-centre load-connection probability
emp.lbl.gov (incl. /queues) returns HTTP 403 to automated requests (probe run 40579353392); eta-publications.lbl.gov serves the same publication page

Workbook layout OBSERVED (GitHub Actions probe run 40615136879 (2026-10-28); sha256 794582d3281c6a305e9615fcfec3fae9dc85be2165216d33760b677e976a08b6, 15,571,236 bytes): 43 visible sheets. '03. Complete Queue Data' (dimension A1:AD38203) is the project-level table: row 1 'RETURN TO CONTENTS', row 2 the 30 column names q_id, q_status, q_date, prop_date, on_date, wd_date, ia_date, IA_phase_raw, IA_phase_clean, county, state, fips_code, poi_name, region, project_name, utility, entity, developer, cluster, service, project_type, type_1, type_2, type_3, type_clean, mw_1, mw_2, mw_3, q_year, prop_year. '04. Data Codebook' (A1:C32; Field Name | Description | Notes) is the data dictionary. Sheets '05'..'40' are report/chart aggregates, not projects.

Codebook rows READ so far: q_id ('Combine with "entity" to form a unique identifier across the full dataset'), q_status ('One of: active, withdrawn, suspended, or operational'), q_date (date project entered queue), prop_date (proposed online date; can be revised), on_date (date became operational, if applicable), wd_date (date withdrawn, if applicable). The remaining codebook rows, incl. units of mw_1..mw_3 and the meaning of type_1..3/type_clean, are UNVERIFIED.

Dates in the project sheet are published as numeric serials (e.g. 43511); the workbook's date epoch flag (date1904) has not been read: the 1900 system is assumed, supported only by q_year agreeing with the serial in all six rows read

Publisher note (sheet '28. IR to WD'): withdrawn date was available for 15,248 requests withdrawn since 2004: withdrawn requests without wd_date exist. In the six rows read, every withdrawn row has a blank wd_date and one operational row has a blank on_date.

The 'sample' notes on aggregate sheets (e.g. 'Sample includes 4,205 projects from 7 ISO/RTOs and 7 non-ISO balancing...') show aggregates use subsets of requests; do not reuse them as denominators for the full table

MEASURED (GitHub Actions probe run 40615868160 (2026-10-28, same workbook sha256 794582d3281c6a305e9615fcfec3fae9dc85be2165216d33760b677e976a08b6)), sheet '03. Complete Queue Data', 38,201 data rows: q_status = withdrawn 24,221 / active 8,513 / operational 4,789 / suspended 668 / unknown 10. The codebook lists only four statuses (no 'unknown'). 665 rows have no q_date (cannot be placed in an entry-year cohort). q_date spans serial 35011..46015 (1995-11-08..2025-12-24); wd_date reaches serial 46038 (2026-01-16); on_date spans 30132..46022 (1982-06-30..2025-12-31) and 63 rows share on_date 2025-12-31, its most common value.

MEASURED status/date quality (same run): 8,639 of 24,221 withdrawn rows (35.7%) have no wd_date; 1,500 of 4,789 operational rows (31.3%) have no on_date; 20 active rows carry a wd_date and 158 active rows carry an on_date; 7 suspended rows carry a wd_date; wd_date < q_date in 6 of 15,414 rows having both; on_date < q_date in 50 of 3,566; on_date < wd_date in 56 of 241. Status-vs-date conflicts therefore exist in the publisher's data and must be flagged, not assumed absent.

MEASURED keys/capacity (same run): the codebook's unique key (entity, q_id) repeats for 135 keys (270 rows; 38,065 distinct keys); 1 row has q_id 'not assigned'. mw_1 is populated in all rows (min -75, max 16,875; units UNVERIFIED); mw_2 is populated in 1,096 rows and mw_3 in 45 (semantics UNVERIFIED). project_type: Generation 36,776, Surplus 100, Upgrade 80, Replacement 21, blank 1,224: not every request is new generation.

MEASURED vocabularies (same run): region 9 values (West 8,097, PJM 7,666, MISO 5,424, Southeast 4,334, ERCOT 3,757, CAISO 2,868, SPP 2,837, NYISO 1,936, ISO-NE 1,282); service NRIS 16,910 / ERIS 5,073 / NRIS/ERIS 4,602 / Other 819 / blank 10,797; type_clean 49 distinct values (Solar 13,479, Wind 6,470, Battery 5,826, Solar+Battery 4,451, Gas 3,744). Whether the 135 repeated keys are identical copies or distinct requests has not yet been measured.

MEASURED (extended; GitHub Actions probe run 40616451452 (2026-10-28, same workbook)): mw_1 has 2 zero and 16 negative values (18 non-positive rows). Additional status/date conflicts: 257 withdrawn rows carry an on_date, 14 operational rows carry a wd_date, 5 suspended rows carry an on_date; all 10 'unknown' rows have neither date. The 135 repeated (entity, q_id) keys are NOT identical copies: 0 are identical, 135 differ (county differs in 134, on_date in 79, ia_date in 35, state in 33): they look like one request listed per county/location, so de-duplicating by key would delete real rows. Capacity IS repeated across such rows (next entry).

MEASURED capacity repetition (GitHub Actions probe run 40638926321, same workbook): in 134 of the 135 repeated (entity, q_id) keys mw_1 is identical on every row; 1 key differs (by 1,000 MW). mw_1 summed over all rows of repeated keys = 53,917.2 and over the non-first rows = 26,458.6 (about 49%). Summing mw_1 over rows therefore double counts roughly 26.5 GW; capacity must be counted once per (entity, q_id). The unit of mw_1 remains UNVERIFIED (codebook rows for it not read).

MEASURED durations/capacity (GitHub Actions probe run 40639536058 (2026-10-28, same workbook); parser version before non-positive-capacity rows were kept): of 38,201 rows 37,518 kept and 683 rejected (665 missing q_date + 18 non-positive mw_1). Years from queue entry to in-service date among OPERATIONAL requests with both dates: all COD years n=3,097 (3,145 minus 48 impossible-order rows; 0 repeated-key rows) median 3.581 y (p25 1.96, p75 5.183); COD 2018-2025 n=1,439 median 4.394 y (p25 3.086, p75 5.844). Conditioned on reaching COD (survivorship). Capacity counted once per (entity, q_id): 6,660,040.7 vs 6,686,499.3 naive (26,458.6 avoided, all on operational rows); by status (deduplicated): withdrawn 4,283,199.4 / active 1,739,387.3 / operational 502,925.4 / suspended 133,561.6 / unknown 967.0 (unit of mw_1 UNVERIFIED).

CROSS-CHECK vs the publisher's own sheet '37. IR to COD - all' (GitHub Actions probe run 40639536058 (2026-10-28, same workbook)): LBNL reports a sample of 3,310 requests (per-in-service-year n for 2005-2025 sums to exactly 3,310; 2018-2025 sums to 1,802) with year medians from 41.9 to 62.7 months in 2018-2025. Our operational-only population (3,145 before exclusions) is smaller than LBNL's 3,310, so the two samples DIFFER by definition: 420 requests carry an in-service date but are not 'operational'. This difference is resolved by the per-COD-year measurement in the next entry.

MEASURED cross-check against the publisher's sheet 37, per in-service year 2005-2025 (GitHub Actions probe run 40640016068 (2026-10-28, same workbook)): requests with BOTH dates regardless of status reproduce LBNL's table closely: our sample is never smaller than LBNL's, exceeding it by 0-4 requests per year (3,339 vs 3,310; +29 residual, cause UNVERIFIED), and where the samples are exactly equal (2009, 2012, 2015, 2016, 2023) our medians match to within 0.005 months; where n differs by 1-4 the medians differ by up to 1.261 months (2014). The residual is a constant ratio of ~1.00008 = 30.44 / 30.4375: LBNL appears to convert days to months at 30.44 days/month while this harness uses 365.25/12. Operational-only reproduces it far worse (2,922 requests vs 3,310; up to 131 fewer in a year: 2025 is 163 vs 294; medians off by up to 4.456 months; total |n difference| 402 vs 29), though it is nearer in n by 1-2 requests in 2006-2008 and 2010. LBNL's exact filter is therefore neither population and remains UNVERIFIED; use population 'has_in_service_date' for LBNL-comparable figures and say so.

sources.name: EIA-930 Hourly Electric Grid Monitor
sources.owner: U.S. Energy Information Administration (data reported by balancing authorities)
sources.release_identity: Rolling; demand ~1h lag, generation ~1 day lag per snippets
sources.semantics: BA-reported hourly electricity demand, demand forecast, net generation and interchange as published by EIA; page documents data quality issues, imputation, pseudo-ties and generation-only BAs
sources.time_convention: Hour-ending: data for the hour ending 1:00 a.m. is reported with a 1:00 a.m. timestamp; values are time-weighted hourly averages; BA data are published in the local time zone chosen by each BA (page has DST reporting and imputation sections). Whether the API also exposes UTC periods is not stated on this page.
sources.geography: Balancing authorities (reporting entities), with regional and sub-regional aggregations per page sections
limitations: Region/BA-level reading is not site-specific headroom
Values may be imputed or revised; see page sections on data quality and imputation
Timestamps are hour-ending in BA-chosen local time on the published page: DST days need explicit handling
Units and licence wording not stated on this page
